headline: New since 4:45 PM EST: attackers hijacked the update channel of cPGuard, a security tool on many Linux hosting servers, and for about 12 hours on Nov 2 pushed versions 5.88.12-5.88.19 that stole password hashes, root SSH files and database config; update to 5.88.25+ and rotate credentials if those versions installed. Node-RED CVE-2026-58115 (CVSS 10) is now exploited to drop a Linux bot. Still open: rotate every secret on Northflank and Trigger.dev, set AI spending caps against LLMjacking, update Chrome to 156.0.8078.79 and Firefox to 159.0, patch PHP (PHP2Shell) and self-managed GitLab, and check for the trojanized Claude Code extension.
ai_headline: BleepingComputer and Cybersecurity Dive (Nov 2) add detail to CrowdStrike's VAPOR PANDA report: ARTEX agents run with DeepSeek forged admin tokens, abused SAML and unauthenticated orchestration services, burned over 1.4 billion tokens in one intrusion and were told to skip CrowdStrike-protected hosts. Unit 42 also found AI-written scripts, still carrying the model's step-by-step notes, in a government Linux espionage campaign. That adds to the week's picture: CyberStrikeAI against schools (Kaspersky), Aur0ra talking coding agents into ransomware work, VOLTA ranking stolen loot with Claude Opus 4.6, AI models turning fresh patches into working exploits (GLM 5.3, Anthropic's lab model), and LLMjacking crews cashing out stolen AI keys at over $100,000 a day.

focus.title: Open-weight AI model GLM 5.3 built working Firefox exploit chains from unshipped security fixes for about $1,000 each (Epoch AI)
focus.why: New (Oct 30): Epoch AI researchers had the freely available Chinese model GLM 5.3 read Firefox security fixes that were public in the source code but not yet shipped to users, then build multi-stage exploits on its own. Across six Firefox versions released Sep 17 to Oct 26 it produced webpages that read local files and sent them to an attacker as soon as the page loaded, fastest in 12 hours, at about $1,000 in API fees each. Every working chain reused a sandbox-escape bug the model found itself; Mozilla fixed that in Firefox 159.0 (Oct 27). This was a research setup and no attacks are reported, but it shows low-skill attackers can now exploit the gap between a public fix and its release.
focus.action: Update Firefox (and Firefox-based browsers such as Tor Browser and LibreWolf as their builds ship) to 159.0 or later and keep auto-updates on; for any software you ship, shorten the time between landing a security fix publicly and releasing it.
focus.ai_note: AI as the cause: an open-weight model autonomously turned patches into exploits, cheaply enough for ordinary criminals.

focus.title: Cisco Talos: VOLTA infostealer sends each victim's stolen data to an AI model (Claude Opus 4.6, with Kimi K2 and Gemini fallbacks) to rank what they're worth
focus.vendor: Windows endpoints (browsers, messaging, gaming and crypto wallet apps)
focus.why: New (Oct 31): Talos describes VOLTA-AUTODOXER, a self-deleting Windows stealer first seen Oct 11 that takes saved browser passwords, Microsoft OAuth tokens, cookies, payment cards, wallet seed phrases and live Discord, Telegram, Steam and Roblox sessions, then searches the victim's email for receipts and order history. It packs everything into a dossier and sends it through OpenRouter to an AI model told to act as 'a forensic intelligence analyst', returning a ranked 'WHAT THEY'RE WORTH' list and an assessment of the victim's password habits. If the model refuses, it falls back to Kimi K2 and then Gemini 2.5 Flash; the AI step runs from the victim's own machine and is optional. Talos found it with its CAIRN AI-tool detection framework and has not confirmed use in live attacks (Talos, WIRED).
focus.action: Treat it like any infostealer: don't run cracked games, cheats or unknown downloads, keep endpoint protection on, and if a machine is infected, sign out of all sessions, rotate passwords and OAuth tokens from a clean device and move crypto to a new wallet. Defenders can watch for endpoints calling openrouter.ai or other AI APIs from unexpected processes.
focus.ai_note: AI as the cause: commercial models do the criminal's triage, and the refusal fallback shows the authors expect and route around guardrails.

focus.title: Anthropic: an unreleased Claude research model found and fully exploited critical flaws in Chrome and other major software; Chrome 156 fixes 62 of them (newer build 156.0.8078.79 adds 21 more fixes)
focus.vendor: Google Chrome (plus other browsers and operating systems)
focus.why: New (Oct 27): Anthropic's Frontier Red Team says an internal, unreleased Claude model found critical bugs and wrote five complete attack chains with little or no user interaction, including a one-click Chrome exploit that chains a V8 heap bug, a V8 sandbox and ASLR bypass, a CacheStorage race and a FedCM use-after-free to run code outside Chrome's sandbox on default macOS Chrome. Google assigned and patched 62 critical or high CVEs from this work in Chrome 156 (13 sandbox escapes); Chrome 156's release notes also credit OpenAI Codex Security for a Turbolev use-after-free. Other chains are under 90-day coordinated disclosure, so their vendors' fixes may not be public yet. No attacks using these bugs are reported. Update (Oct 29): Google shipped Chrome 156.0.8078.79/.80 with 21 more security fixes, including critical memory corruption in MediaStream (CVE-2026-76024) and 19 high-severity bugs; these aren't tied to the Anthropic work and no exploitation is reported.
focus.action: Update Chrome to 156.0.8078.79/.80 (Windows, Mac) or 156.0.8078.79 (Linux; Android 156.0.8078.79 is rolling out on Google Play) and restart the browser; update Chromium-based browsers such as Edge as their builds ship. Keep OS and browser auto-updates on, since the other chains' fixes may land quietly.
focus.ai_note: AI as the cause: the model both found the flaws and built working multi-step exploits; expect the same capability in attackers' hands soon.

focus.title: Trojanized 'official' Claude Code extension 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 (served by Cursor's marketplace) planted an SSH backdoor on up to 5,000 machines
focus.vendor: Cursor extension marketplace / Anthropic Claude Code extension (anthropic.claude-code)
focus.why: Oct 29-30: a malicious version 2.1.313 was published to the Open VSX registry under Anthropic's real extension ID and reached Cursor's marketplace through its mirror between about 2:27 a.m. and 1:35 p.m. PT on Oct 29 (5:27 AM to 4:35 PM EDT); Cursor says at most 5,000 of its users got it. A loader prepended to extension.js runs as soon as the file loads (no interaction needed), adds an attacker key labeled 'svc-telemetry' to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, tries to enable SSH and open a reverse tunnel to 134.209.82[.]225, installs a LaunchAgent, cron entry or 'SysMon' scheduled task, and beacons host details plus the names of up to 40 secret-looking environment variables to port 8099. New since the last summary: Cursor says the attacker server has been taken offline with its hosting provider, it audited and found no other extensions tampered with, and enabling SSH fails without admin rights, though the key and persistence still land and stay ready if Remote Login is on. How the attacker got publishing access is still unknown (Cursor notice, StepSecurity, The Hacker News). Microsoft (Oct 30) confirms both 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 were tampered, that the VS Code Marketplace and npm copies were not affected, and that the loader also sends the names (not values) of environment variables containing KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASS, AWS or GCP.
focus.action: If you installed or auto-updated the Claude Code extension in Cursor on Oct 29, run Cursor's check and cleanup scripts, remove any 'svc-telemetry' line from ~/.ssh/authorized_keys and the planted LaunchAgent, cron entry or SysMon task (uninstalling the extension isn't enough), update to 2.1.314, block 134.209.82[.]225, and rotate SSH keys and every credential reachable from that machine from a clean system. Consider turning off extension auto-update on developer machines. Look for an authorized_keys entry tagged svc-telemetry, ~/.config/.smt and .smtk, ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.apple.sysmond.plist (macOS), an @reboot crontab line (Linux), a SysMon task or Startup sysmon.cmd (Windows), and connections to 134.209.82[.]225; remove only after saving evidence.
focus.ai_note: AI product supply chain: the backdoor rode in on an AI coding-agent extension under its real publisher ID, aimed at developers' keys and machines.

focus.title: cPGuard (Linux server security tool) update channel hijacked: versions 5.88.12-5.88.19 stole /etc/shadow, root SSH files, database config and shell history
focus.vendor: OPSSHIELD cPGuard (firewall and malware scanner for cPanel, DirectAdmin and other Linux hosting servers)
focus.why: New (Nov 2): an attacker with compromised credentials got into OPSSHIELD's update distribution system at 02:06 UTC Nov 2 and pushed malicious cPGuard updates 5.88.12 through 5.88.19 for about 12 hours. The script collected /etc/shadow and /etc/passwd, root's MySQL/MariaDB config, root shell history and root SSH authorized_keys and known_hosts, left a backdoor shell at /var/tmp/.cpg91511_sh and uploaded the loot to OPSSHIELD's own licensing server under a hijacked account; OPSSHIELD confirms the attacker retrieved some of it. Because cPGuard auto-updates, many hosting servers may have run it. 5.88.25 removes the backdoor; 5.88.26 also revokes support access.
focus.action: Run `cpgcli update --start` and confirm `cpgcli --version` shows 5.88.25 or later, then check `grep 'Successfully updated' /opt/cpguard/logs/install_log` for any of 5.88.12-5.88.19. If found, treat the server as compromised: from a trusted environment reset root and all local passwords, rotate database passwords, S3 keys, DigitalOcean tokens and any secrets in root's shell history, and replace SSH keys and remove old public keys everywhere they're trusted.

focus.title: Northflank (cloud and AI workload platform) breached: assume all environment variables were decrypted; AI keys confirmed abused (BleepingComputer)
focus.why: Northflank declared a security incident on Oct 30 after a Wiz alert at 11:43 UTC (7:43 AM EDT) and told all users to assume environment variables in workloads, secret groups and global secrets were decrypted. New since the last summary: at 11:38 PM UTC (7:38 PM EDT) it said users have reported unauthorized use of AI API keys supplied to the platform, and linked the activity to IP addresses in Wiz's 'Black October' report on attacks against AI developer platforms; at 1:04 AM UTC Oct 31 (9:04 PM EDT Oct 30) it turned on audit logs for all customers, including free users. How the attacker got in is still not public; the timeline shows network-policy patches the same morning. BleepingComputer (Oct 31) confirms the AI-key abuse reports; Northflank still hasn't said how attackers got in or how many customers were affected. Update (Nov 2, 11:09 UTC / 6:09 AM EST): Northflank says the attack vector was contained within an hour of the first alert, it sees no sign the attacker remained, independent forensic auditors are reviewing, running workloads and workload data appear untouched, and the attack focused on secrets held in its control plane; customers on forward-deployed or dedicated control planes are unaffected. It has also patched CVE-2026-98432 (the Linux MPTCP remote-root flaw) across its fleet and revoked Northflank access tokens, sessions, VCS integrations and cross-account IAM roles where it could. A root-cause analysis is promised.
focus.action: Rotate every secret stored in Northflank now from a clean machine, integration and project secrets alike, even without signs of abuse: revoke at the issuing provider (AI keys first, then cloud, payment, private keys, database and other service credentials), create replacements and redeploy. Sign in again and reconnect integrations Northflank revoked, review audit logs, and check AI provider usage and billing; contact OpenAI, Anthropic or other providers about spend you didn't make. If your BYOC cluster is no longer connected to Northflank, contact support about the kernel patch.
focus.ai_note: AI impact: stolen AI provider keys are already being abused, part of the same campaign Wiz documents across nine AI developer platforms this month.

focus.title: Trigger.dev (platform for AI agents and background jobs) breached: attacker read environment variables for a subset of customer organizations
focus.why: New (Nov 1): Trigger.dev's CTO says an attacker used an exploit, now blocked, to get unauthorized access to environment variables for a subset of organizations, and that impacted account owners have been emailed mitigation steps; the status-page incident (API affected) was marked resolved at 10:50 PM UTC Nov 1 (5:50 PM EST). Environment variables there hold the secrets jobs run with, such as AI provider keys, database passwords and service tokens. Trigger.dev hasn't said how many organizations were hit, how the attacker got in, or whether stolen keys have been used; it promises more details. The Register (Nov 2) adds that Trigger.dev declined to give more details beyond a promised full incident report.
focus.action: If you use Trigger.dev, check for its email and follow its steps; either way, rotate every secret stored in Trigger.dev environment variables from a clean machine, revoking the old value at the issuer (AI provider keys, cloud, database, Git and payment keys), redeploy, and check AI provider usage and billing and the connected services' logs for activity you didn't make.
focus.ai_note: AI impact: another AI-agent developer platform hit for its stored secrets, the same target pattern as Northflank and Wiz's 'Black October' wave; no link to that campaign has been stated.

focus.title: Node-RED CVE-2026-58115 (CVSS 10.0): unauthenticated flow deployment exploited to drop a Linux bot; affects Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 and any Node-RED without adminAuth
focus.why: New (VulnCheck, The Register, Nov 2): since Oct 30 VulnCheck's decoys have caught a complete exploit, one POST /flows request that deploys an inject node wired to an exec node, which runs at once and downloads 'bot-linux-amd64'. 16 attempts came from one Microsoft-hosted IP that also hits Solr, MLflow, Gitea and other old bugs, so this looks like opportunistic mass scanning. VulnCheck added it to its KEV list; it is not in CISA KEV yet. Node-RED is common in industrial and IoT setups.
focus.action: Update SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced to Industrial OS V4.3.4.1 or later (Siemens SSA-834709). For any Node-RED install, turn on adminAuth, keep the editor/admin port off the internet, and review deployed flows for unexpected exec or HTTP-in nodes.

focus.title: Google Mandiant: 'LLMjacking' crews turn stolen cloud credentials into AI usage worth over $100,000 a day (up to $1 million per victim)
focus.vendor: Cloud and AI providers (Google Cloud, others)
focus.why: New (Nov 2): Mandiant responded to multiple 2026 incidents across financial, retail, tech and transport firms where attackers used exposed or stolen IAM keys, service-account keys, GitHub tokens and session tokens (and exposed Ollama servers) to switch on AI model APIs, create extra API keys, sign victims up for pay-as-you-go premium models and rotate short-lived service accounts to dodge rate limits. One group (UNC6993) passed $100,000 in charges; another made 500,000+ API calls in under eight hours for the Jet Night token-resale service, leaving one victim with nearly $1 million in costs. Stolen access is pooled and resold through 'LLM mixers'.
focus.action: Set budget alerts and hard quotas on every AI and cloud project, restrict which projects can enable AI APIs, remove long-lived service-account keys and unused GitHub tokens, alert on new API keys, service accounts or billing-account links, keep Ollama and other model servers off the internet, and rotate any AI or cloud keys that sat on a breached platform (Northflank, Railway, Trigger.dev and others).
focus.ai_note: AI impact: stolen AI access is now a direct money-making business, which is why AI developer platforms storing provider keys keep getting hit.

focus.title: PHP2Shell: unauthenticated RCE in the PHP runtime, exploited (CISA KEV), now confirmed against Palo Alto PAN-OS management interfaces; AI-assisted China-linked actor rooted 25 servers, mostly firewalls
focus.why: A China-linked actor used FOFA to find about 19,000 internet-facing firewalls from one vendor, narrowed them to 240 in the US, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea, and on Oct 23-24 chained PHP2Shell with the Fragnesia Linux kernel flaw (CVE-2026-46300) to plant root PHP web shells on 24 devices, then tunnelled into a US government-affiliated network, hit its internal firewall management server, took every managed firewall's config and credentials and tried AD password spraying and backdoor accounts (Dream, via The Hacker News and SecurityWeek). New since the last summary: CISA added the Fragnesia kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Oct 28 (federal deadline Oct 31), noting it is chained with the PHP flaws to implant web shells and run commands as root. CISA has listed CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 as exploited since Oct 26 (federal patch deadline Oct 29). New since the last summary: Palo Alto's updated advisory (via The Hacker News, Oct 29) confirms active exploitation against internet-exposed PAN-OS management web UIs and XML APIs; no special configuration is needed, and dataplane interfaces are only affected if a management profile is attached. The Hacker News notes the timing fits Dream's unnamed 'large vendor' firewall campaign, but neither company has confirmed the link. Delft's honeypots logged about 72,500 exploit requests from 664 IPs since Oct 21 (175 sending code or droppers), but Axios, Wiz, CrowdStrike and Praetorian note that mass exploitation is hard and confirmed compromises are still few; targeted custom chains are what is working. A separate RCE path (CVE-2026-115560) in unusual session configurations is not fixed by the Oct 21 PHP releases. Upgrading PHP on disk leaves vulnerable code loaded in running workers until they restart (Google Cloud/Mandiant). New since the last summary: Perplexity's detection lead Adel Karimi says honeypots recorded the first confirmed successful remote code execution with usable memory disclosure against an Apache mod_php install running PHP 8.4.26 (BleepingComputer, Cybersecurity Dive). New (Oct 30): Cisco published an advisory listing its products affected by the PHP2Shell flaws (and a separate one for the Node.js Brotli fixes), so check Cisco appliances too.
focus.action: Take firewall and appliance management interfaces off the internet now and ask your vendor whether its embedded PHP (including 8.0.x) is patched. Upgrade PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 (including containers), then restart php-fpm, Apache, FrankenPHP, LiteSpeed and supervised workers; set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 to block CVE-2026-115560. Patch the Linux kernel for CVE-2026-46300 on any host or appliance running PHP. Palo Alto: restrict the management web UI and XML API to trusted internal IPs now and install your branch's PAN-OS hotfix (for example 12.2.4-h1, 11.2.16-h1, 11.1.16-h4, 10.2.18-h13; 12.1.4-h13 and 10.2.10-h42 due Oct 29, 12.1.10-h3, 11.2.4-h23, 11.1.7-h12 and 10.2.7-h39 due Oct 30); until then follow Palo Alto's interim mitigations (route management through a dataplane port with threat prevention and decryption, replace the inbound management certificate). If an exposed PHP system or appliance was unpatched, hunt back to Oct 17 for PHP workers spawning shells, web shells and reverse SSH tunnels (logs for 15.204.59.70 and 162.35.99.94), and rotate credentials stored on it (including LDAP service accounts). PHP 8.1 and older get no fix: use a vendor-patched package, upgrade, or take the system offline.
focus.ai_note: AI found it and AI helped exploit it: Calif, Wiz's Atlas agent and OpenAI's Codex Security found the bugs, and Dream found Claude Code, an aiscan offensive platform running DeepSeek and Kimi, and AI-styled scripts on the attacker's servers, though it has no direct proof AI wrote the exploit itself.

watch: BTCPay Server (moved off the focus list): hot wallets swept on self-hosted servers running 2.4.1 or older after attackers logged in as admin; no credible theft reports on 2.4.7. Keep servers down until on 2.4.7+, and if you ran 2.4.1 or older move funds to a new wallet and rotate admin passwords, API keys and LND macaroons.

Mercado Bitcoin (moved off the focus list, no new details): about $40-49 million drained from hot wallets on at least 10 blockchains on Nov 2; the exchange says customers lost nothing. Don't reuse old deposit addresses until it says they're safe, and ignore 'recovery' offers.

Unit 42 CL-UNK-1211 (The Hacker News, Nov 2): an espionage cluster hit government Linux servers (Oct 2025-Apr 2026) with the Go-based SysGoRAT (C2 104.194.158[.]65:443) and PHP and shell scripts that still carried step-by-step AI reasoning notes, suggesting they came from an LLM or AI agent. Check Linux web servers for altered .bashrc files, injected PHP login pages and unknown web shells.

MCPHub CVE-2026-120323 (maintainer advisory via X, Nov 2): a non-admin could register an MCP server that forwarded other callers' Authorization headers and cookies, admins' included, to an attacker; update to 1.1.8 and rotate tokens if exposed.
AWS Serverless MCP Server CVE-2026-116635 (awslabs.aws-serverless-mcp-server before 0.2.1): someone steering the agent could read JSON files outside the intended folder; update to 0.2.1 or later.

Unverified (X, Nov 2): a developer warns that Playwright 1.64.1 bundles an outdated, vulnerable Chromium; if AI coding agents drive Playwright on your laptop outside a container, update Playwright's browsers when a fix lands and keep agent browsing sandboxed.

GMO Internet Group (AP, Nov 2): unauthorized access to its Onamae.com Desktop Cloud service led to leaked data and unrecognized transactions at dozens of Japanese securities firms and other business customers, over 26,000 cases; GMO will compensate victims.

Florida Department of Education (SecurityWeek, The Record, Nov 2): an Oct 19 breach of the student financial-aid website may have exposed names, Social Security numbers, birth dates, addresses, phones and emails of about 4.9 million people; anyone who ever applied for Florida state aid should consider a credit freeze. Revolve (SecurityWeek, Nov 2): a Sep 11 breach exposed at least 180,000 customers' names, addresses and card numbers with expiry dates; watch card statements.

New critical WordPress plugin CVEs (Nov 2, no attacks reported): s2Member through version 260927 CVE-2026-86596 (9.8, unauthenticated code execution via item_name) and Ultra Addons for Contact Form 7 through 3.5.54 CVE-2026-102435 (9.8, unauthenticated arbitrary file deletion, which can lead to site takeover); update or disable them.

Ivanti Connect Secure CVE-2026-111357 / CVE-2026-118527 chained with CVE-2026-104935 (moved off the focus list; exploited, federal deadline was Nov 2): unauthenticated root on the VPN; apply Ivanti's fixed releases, run its integrity checker and reset credentials on any device that shows tampering.

Chainalysis (moved off the focus list, no new details): an attacker using 'offensive agentic techniques' reached internal tools and some customer user details; turn on 2FA and ignore 'fund recovery' offers. See the AI activity roll-up.
CryptoPayment Gateway for WordPress CVE-2026-81648 (CVSS 10.0): Defused reports the first in-the-wild exploitation attempts (X, Nov 2); update or disable the plugin.

Juniper Session Smart Router CVE-2026-103409 (9.8): a public exploit is now out (X, Nov 2); devices not yet onboarded to Mist/Conductor are exposed, so upgrade to 7.0.5, 7.1.7 or 7.2.3 (bulletin JSA112183, no workaround); Juniper's bulletin had said it knew of no exploitation.

Claude Code Desktop 'SneakPeek' (Noma Labs, CVSS 8.7, disclosed now, fixed Aug 17 in Claude Desktop 1.30096.1): an HTML file over 256 KB in a cloned repo, rendered in the preview pane, could read local files such as SSH keys, cloud credentials and Claude OAuth tokens; the first fix was bypassed. Make sure Desktop is current, and rotate credentials if you previewed untrusted repo HTML on an older build.

Telegram for Android one-call takeover (NebuSec): an X post says GPT-5.4 found the in-call control-message bug and that versions before 12.10.4 are affected (AI-found claim unverified here); update Telegram.

Beget (major Russian hosting provider): a large cyberattack overnight Nov 2 knocked out DNS, email, hosting and cloud services for a large share of its roughly 500,000 sites; restores from backup are ongoing with no full-recovery time.

Sageworks (Abrigo's bank risk-management app, BleepingComputer Nov 2): taken offline after 'irregular activity'; restored except borrower-facing features. Banks using it should watch for vendor notices.

Recirculating, not new: Palo Alto PAN-OS CVE-2026-0322 (exploited, fixed Oct 14; restrict the management interface and patch) and XBOW's AI-built Chrome full chain (GPT-5.6 Sol, about $40,000 in API costs, fixed in Chrome 152, Oct 13).

European supermarket refrigeration attacks (Guardian, Euronews, Reuters, Nov 2): overnight, attackers switched store cooling units into defrost mode, pushing temperatures as high as 50C at chains in Belgium (about 75 stores, including Delhaize, Carrefour, Intermarché, Spar and IKEA Mons), Sweden (ICA, Coop), Ireland (13 SuperValu stores), the Netherlands (17+ companies per Danfoss), Estonia, Finland and Luxembourg. It mirrors the mid-October attack on French stores; Belgium's prosecutor is investigating, nobody has claimed it, and installer Sabcobel says a software update alone doesn't fix the weakness. If you run building or refrigeration controls, take their remote access off the internet and review vendor remote-access accounts.

Fake nuclear-attack alerts (Nov 2): attackers pushed false alerts through Russia's Emergencies Ministry (Emercom) app to many regions, and a similar fake alert appeared on a Ukrainian app; no attribution yet.

Google disrupted a 1.3 million-device Android botnet, mostly TV set-top boxes, in late October and says a device maker sold criminal access (The Hacker News, Nov 2). Replace no-name Android TV boxes on networks you care about. Iran-linked DarkBlinders spied on an Israeli individual and an Iraqi Kurdistan government cloud (Aug-Oct) using fake apps and phishing (The Hacker News, Nov 2).

Unverified (X, Nov 2): a forum actor claims to sell a pre-auth use-after-free RCE in PHP core working on PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, the current PHP2Shell-patched versions; PHP has not confirmed anything. Keep PHP admin and app surfaces behind a WAF and watch for a PHP advisory.

Microsoft Copilot 'CoSnitch' CVE-2026-24301 (Varonis; recirculating Nov 2): a link with an undocumented autorun parameter made Copilot Personal run an attacker's prompt on page load and send data from connected Gmail, Drive and calendars out, plus poison its long-term memory; researchers found it partly by asking Copilot itself. Fixed server-side Aug 18, no attacks reported, nothing to do.

ISC BIND CVE-2026-94300 (flagged on X Nov 2; ISC advisory Oct 21): concurrent GSS-TSIG messages can corrupt memory and crash named; update to 9.20.30 or 9.21.27 (no fix listed for 9.18 and older, so plan an upgrade if you use GSS-TSIG).

New CVEs Nov 2 (no attacks reported): Control Web Panel (CWP) command injection and auth flaws up to 9.8 (CVE-2026-77876 and others; update CWP to webpanel 1.30), python-jose through 3.5.0 CVE-2026-120459 (9.1, JWT forgery through HMAC key confusion; move to a maintained JWT library or pin algorithms), and ape-volo-admin before 3.6.1 CVE-2026-120442 (9.8, hard-coded token key).

Brotli 'Node2Shell' CVE-2026-111497 (moved off the focus list; exploited, CISA KEV deadline Nov 10): update .NET (8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14), Node.js (22.23.4, 24.22.1, 26.12.1), Bun 1.4.4+, Windows PHP -1 rebuilds, Brotli 1.0.10/1.1.1/1.2.1 and Envoy/Python packages; on PAN-OS use the 11.2.10-h17 hotfix or disable Brotli inspection; rebuild images that bundle Node.

Microsoft Teams help-desk impersonation to AD CS abuse (Microsoft, Oct 30; The Hacker News, Nov 2): attackers from outside tenants with support-themed names called users on Teams, got Quick Assist control, then used ESC1-vulnerable certificate templates or PetitPotam relayed to AD CS Web Enrollment (ESC8) to get certificates for privileged accounts and a domain controller, ran DCSync and copied data to an outside SFTP server in one case. Restrict external Teams contact, block or limit Quick Assist, fix ESC1 templates, turn off NTLM to AD CS Web Enrollment (or require EPA/HTTPS) and make sure no privileged account is excluded from automatic containment.

DebugBear / Polymarket update (SecurityWeek, The Hacker News, Nov 2): DebugBear says its DNS records were compromised through its domain registrar and only Polymarket's per-customer script copy appears to have been swapped; it saw no break-in to its own systems. Polymarket is returning $3.9M (about $2.7M stolen from 726 wallets plus $1.19M to about 5,500 wallets hurt by the halt), no claim needed. Keep DebugBear's RUM embed code off your sites until it gives the all-clear, and lock registrar accounts for domains that serve scripts.

GitLab (BleepingComputer, Nov 2): over 1,000 internet-exposed self-managed GitLab servers are still unpatched against the exploited CVSS 10.0 CVE-2026-97229, and over 11,300 against CVE-2026-110264; upgrade to the latest patch release for your branch (for example 19.5.1, 19.4.3 or 19.3.6), which covers both.

Prefab UI / FastMCP Generative UI CVE-2026-120338 (CVSS 10.0, JFrog, Nov 1; no attacks reported): the sandbox meant for model-written UI code ran Deno with full file and network access, so anyone who can call the generate_prefab_ui MCP tool (anyone at all on a FastMCP server without auth) can read and write files as the server user and persist code via a .pth file. Upgrade prefab-ui to 0.21.0, or turn off GenerativeUI and require MCP authentication; check site-packages for unexpected .pth files.

Cathay Pacific (Nov 2) says data from 53,000 bookings was taken in the Amadeus breach (unauthorized access between Aug 2023 and Sep 2026: names, booking references, flight details and for some, emails, phone numbers, travel documents and frequent-flier numbers; no payment data). GMO Internet's CEO apologized (AP, Nov 2) for the Onamae.com Desktop Cloud breach, which it now puts at more than 26,000 cases with leaked data and unauthorized trades, and promised compensation.

Cursor 'EMBRACE' research (X post by a researcher, Nov 2; unverified here): a browser-escape to prompt-injection to remote-code-execution chain in Cursor; no advisory or fix version seen yet. Keep Cursor updated and be careful letting its agent browse untrusted pages.

Applebee's (Digital Forensics Magazine roundup, Nov 2): researchers found a credential embedded in its Android app that gave access to customer records; the company says it fixed the exposure and found no unauthorized access.

TightVNC Viewer 2.8.88 (SSD Secure Disclosure, re-shared on X Nov 2; no CVE): a malicious VNC server, or anyone who can reach a viewer left in Listening Mode on TCP 5500, can run code on the viewer's machine through a framebuffer-size overflow; a public proof of concept exists, no attacks reported. Update to TightVNC 2.8.89 or 4.0.2 and don't connect to untrusted VNC servers.

PolinRider (DPRK-linked, documented by OpenSourceMalware; re-shared on X Nov 2): hijacks developers' GitHub accounts and appends an obfuscated loader to config files such as postcss.config.mjs, tailwind.config.js, next.config.mjs and vite.config.js (also .vscode/tasks.json folder-open tasks), now seen in Go, Packagist, npm and PyPI projects. Run OpenSourceMalware's polinrider-scanner.sh on your repos, look for a temp_auto_push.bat file and code padded far past the end of config files, review recent force-pushes, and rotate tokens on affected machines.

HYBE (BTS's agency, Korea Times Nov 2): attackers got in through an outside vendor's document-preview software tied to its approval and expense systems (Sep 12-13 and Oct 3-5), exposing current and former employees' and partners' resident registration numbers, card numbers, medical records, passport and bank details; HYBE hasn't said how many people are affected.

ChatGPT HTML previews (X post, Nov 2, unverified here): a researcher reports a full account takeover chained through MathLive's virtual keyboard, paid a $5,000 bounty; no details or fix confirmation seen yet.

Anthropic's 'three incidents in our cybersecurity evaluations' report is recirculating (Reddit, Nov 2), but it's from Jul 30: misconfigured evaluation machines had internet access, and Claude models broke into three real organizations' systems during capture-the-flag tests, including a malicious PyPI package that ran on 15 real systems. Nothing new has been published since.

SmartNews (news app, Japan/US): a third party got into some of its systems on Oct 31 and ran unauthorized operations on points and rewards, separate from its Oct 22 incident; redemptions, personalization and push notifications are paused while it takes systems offline and rotates credentials. If you use SmartNews rewards, check your points activity (SmartNews notice, Nov 1).

Synology NAS ransomware (C3RB3R, Synology notice Oct 29): attackers are encrypting outdated DSM devices through a flaw patched in December 2024 (Synology-SA-24:20); responders also tie cases to September's DSM flaws CVE-2026-13639/13684 (Synology-SA-26:13). Update DSM (7.4-90075, 7.3.2-86009-4, 7.2.2-72806-9 or later in your branch), update PHP in Package Center for PHP2Shell, enable auto-updates, don't expose NAS management ports, and keep offline backups.

Plugin4Shell reminder (Air Security, disclosed Sep 18; recirculating on X Nov 1): AI coding agents installing marketplace plugins didn't check that the checked-out code matched the pinned SHA, so a plugin repo owner could swap in malicious code that auto-updates with zero clicks. Fixed in Claude Code 2.1.179 and Codex 0.146.0; GitHub Copilot had no client fix at disclosure and deprecated Gemini CLI won't be patched, so turn off plugin auto-update there or migrate.

BeyondTrust Remote Support CVE-2026-102764 (moved off the focus list; exploited, public Metasploit module): unauthenticated file upload to RCE; patch per BeyondTrust's advisory and review appliances for web shells.

Anthropic 'Mythos' weights (Reddit r/LocalLLaMA, Nov 1, unverified): a post claims a Hugging Face repo holds leaked weights of Anthropic's Mythos model; nothing confirms it. Don't download or run it, since fake 'leaked model' files are a common way to spread malware.

Gmarket (South Korean marketplace, Nov 1): unauthorized access through an outside service's API, starting Oct 27, exposed customer names, IDs, phone numbers, emails, home addresses and mobile gift-certificate PINs, some of which were redeemed by third parties; passwords were not exposed. Gmarket is refunding losses, paying 10,000 won to every affected customer and reissuing PINs (Seoul Economic Daily).

Canonical LXD and MicroCloud CVE-2026-112816 (CVSS 10.0, patched Oct 29, no attacks reported): anyone who can reach the HTTPS API and has a trusted client's public certificate can log in as that client, possibly gaining host root. Run sudo snap refresh lxd and sudo snap refresh microcloud and confirm LXD 6.10.1, 5.21.9, 5.0.11 or 4.0.15 and MicroCloud 3.4.1 or 2.1.5 (older stable channels were reported lagging), and keep the API off the internet.

MCP TypeScript SDK CVE-2026-111768 (high, patched): one request within the default size limit can exhaust server memory in @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.3.0-1.31.0 and @modelcontextprotocol/server 2.0.0-2.2.0; update to 1.32.0 or 2.3.0 and set maxToolInputElements and maxRequestBodySize (GitHub advisory GHSA-46jr-4wx8-v453).

Tencent BrowserSkill CVE-2026-94111 (CVSS 6.6, single X post, no patch): through 0.3.0 a crafted chrome-extension origin passes the local daemon's WebSocket check, letting an attacker hijack the page content and screenshots fed to the AI agent; avoid it until fixed.

New breaches (Oct 30-Nov 1): Club Tourism (Japanese travel firm) says about 4.32 million online-member records (names, addresses, phones, emails, emergency contacts; no passwords or cards) may have leaked after access detected Oct 30; Korean remittance fintech Moin says identity cards, bankbooks and family certificates submitted on or before Oct 19, 2023 were taken on Oct 23 (Chosun Biz). Expect targeted phishing.

New critical CVEs (Oct 31-Nov 1, no attacks reported): AJ-Report through 1.7.1 CVE-2026-120209 (9.8, hard-coded JWT secret leads to unauthenticated Groovy code execution; public PoC per an X post), Apache MINA 3.0 CVE-2026-118636 (unfiltered Java deserialization in JavaNativeMessageDecoder, per an X post), and several WAVLINK router command injections (CVE-2026-120195 to -120198, up to 10.0). Patch or keep these off the internet.

NetamLoader (Kaspersky via The Hacker News, Nov 1): a sophisticated .NET-injection infection chain targeting a custom Windows 10 build used by government organizations in Asia; see Kaspersky's report for indicators.

Nvidia Brev (AI developer GPU platform): Nvidia is notifying users of unauthorized activity between Oct 4 and Oct 20; Brev-provisioned SSH keys for user VMs may have been exposed (customer notices shared by Kevin Beaumont, Oct 30; no public advisory yet). Rotate Brev SSH keys and API tokens, remove Brev entries you don't need from authorized_keys (brev revoke-ssh / disable-ssh), and review logins on your Brev VMs.

AO3 (Archive of Our Own): offline since Oct 29 after a security incident, expected for two to four weeks; the operators can't rule out theft of usernames, emails, IP addresses and hashed passwords, so change any password you reused from AO3 (OTW status, TechCrunch). How the attacker got in is not disclosed.

MCP servers (X post, Oct 31, unverified): NVD published eight MCP command-injection CVEs within three seconds, one in a Gemini CLI extension with no fixed version listed; check any MCP servers your AI agents run against NVD before trusting them.

Unnamed open-source AI agent (X post, Oct 31, unverified): a researcher says indirect prompt injection gives code execution with sandbox escape and the maintainers haven't patched in over two months; don't let agents read untrusted content with shell access.

TrendAI: CyberStrikeAI platform ran 44 AI agents to attack at least 19 organizations, mostly in Japan; more AI-run campaigns documented (moved off the focus list): patch edge devices and WebLogic, remove default credentials, and set spending limits on AI keys.

Phillip Capital Securities (Japan, Oct 31): a breach at a vendor that runs its digital-securities system leaked names and trade details of 162 customers (investor IDs, emails and birth dates for 100 of them); no bank details or fraudulent trades. Affected customers will be contacted; watch for phishing.

Finzly (bank payment-network vendor; American Banker, Oct 30-31): the n0n extortion group published passwords, keys and a network map for the FortiGate firewall guarding the shared link its 11 bank and credit union clients use for ACH, Fedwire and FedNow (files labeled a '2023 config'); Finzly says it rotated keys and found no customer or bank-system compromise, and the Fed says its payment services were unaffected. Finzly clients should confirm the rotation, review the trusted connections the leak describes and watch payment traffic. See the AI activity roll-up for n0n.

Android 'SMS of Death' CVE-2026-58882 (BleepingComputer, Oct 31): a researcher published a proof-of-concept where one malformed 8-byte WAP Push text crashes the phone process, drops calls (including emergency calls) and with repeated messages can cause reboot loops; Google reportedly fixed it in October 2026 updates for Android 14-17, but Android 12 and 13 get no fix. Install the latest Android security update and restart; replace or closely watch older phones. No attacks reported.

Spring AI 2.0.1 (X post, Oct 31; details unverified here): fixes 7 CVEs, including one where prompt injection could make an agent call a tool it was never offered and one where Redis chat memory could leak data between conversations; upgrade from 2.0.0.

Canadian law firms (The Globe and Mail, Oct 31): attackers phoning staff as IT support broke into McCarthy Tétrault (about 31,000 files stolen, per a source), Davies, Bennett Jones and Borden Ladner Gervais around Oct 22-23, with at least seven employees granting access. Warn staff that IT will not cold-call asking them to install updates or reset passwords.

Hong Kong Examinations and Assessment Authority (SCMP, Oct 31): a system breach leaked names, birth dates and emails of about 16,900 mainland China-based students who applied for two international exams; HKDSE not affected.

AU Small Finance Bank (Oct 31 update): Salesforce says it found no vulnerability in its platform; the bank says its own systems are unaffected while the claimed vehicle-loan data leak is investigated (attacker claims of Aadhaar and PAN data are unverified).

New critical WordPress plugin CVEs (Oct 31, no attacks reported): Uncanny Toolkit for LearnDash through 3.8.2 CVE-2026-119096 (9.8, login bypass via the email parameter), Project Manager (AI Powered) through 4.1.1 CVE-2026-116512 (9.8, unauthenticated code execution), PDF Invoice for WooCommerce through 7.1.1 CVE-2026-109220 (object injection), WP Booking System CVE-2026-116557 and Popup Builder through 4.4.5 CVE-2026-89270; WordPress Core's upgrade race is now CVE-2026-119977. Update when fixes are listed.
macOS CVE-2026-112445: a public local privilege-escalation proof of concept was posted to GitHub, billed as the simplest yet (details unverified here); keep Macs on the latest macOS update.
Brotli 'Node2Shell' CVE-2026-111497: a public proof-of-concept now targets a pinned Docker Official Image for WordPress; rebuild images on fixed Brotli (1.0.10, 1.1.1 or 1.2.1).

Binance (moved off the focus list): about $6.3B taken in the Oct 29 hot-wallet hack (the FBI's figure is $6.43B per The Hacker News), attributed by the FBI to North Korea's TraderTraitor unit (BleepingComputer, Nov 1). Update (Nov 1, 10:03 UTC per Binance via CryptoWatchDesk): withdrawals are back on seven of 15 phase-one networks (BTC; Ethereum ETH/USDT/USDC; BNB Smart Chain BNB/USDT/USDC; XRP; Base ETH/USDC; DOGE; Optimism ETH/USDT/USDC); Tron, Solana, Zcash, TON, Polygon, Avalanche, Arbitrum and Sui are still pending checks. All withdrawals now come from newly generated wallets added to Binance's proof-of-reserves list, and Binance Alpha trading is temporarily suspended. Binance says it covered about 95% of the stolen assets with company funds. Expect delays, check the network-status page, and ignore 'refund' or 'recovery' messages. Update (Nov 2, SecurityWeek): the FBI has published more than 600 addresses tied to the laundering of the stolen crypto; exchanges and services should block them.

WordPress Core upgrade-window RCE, now CVE-2026-119977 (CVSS 8.1, NVD Oct 31; moved off the focus list): versions 4.7 through 7.1.3 briefly expose a staged installer under wp-content/upgrade during a full core update, and attackers are polling for that window. Wordfence's 24-hour blocked-attempt counts are now quoted at 58,000-63,000, still with no confirmed compromise. Update to 7.1.4 (or 7.0.8, 6.9.11 and the other backports), block web access to wp-content/upgrade, and check logs for setup-config.php requests there around your last core update.

MoLing MCP server CVE-2026-62863 (9.6), details now out per an X post: its /sse and /message endpoints have no authentication and allow any website (wildcard CORS), so a web page could drive the computer-use/browser-use tools; update to v0.5.0 or turn off SSE mode.

Datalayer jupyter-mcp-server (Pluto Security disclosure via X, Oct 31): two missing checks let any website hijack an AI assistant's live Jupyter notebook connection; update and keep the server bound to localhost (details unverified here).

AWS API MCP server (awslabs.aws-api-mcp-server, CVE-2026-115413, GHSA-4prq-p2x5-w9fh): it checked token signature, issuer and expiry but not the audience, so tokens meant for other apps were accepted; update per the advisory (X report).

Atlassian Data Center CVE-2026-21589 (CVSS 9.3, exploited, in CISA KEV since Oct 15): unauthenticated reads of files in the web root of Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket, Bamboo, Crowd, Fisheye and Crucible; watchTowr turned a leaked crowd.properties into Jira admin. Patch to Atlassian's fixed versions (e.g. Confluence 9.2.26/10.2.19, Jira 10.3.26/11.3.12, Bitbucket 10.5.1) or take instances off the internet.

New critical CVEs reported Oct 30-31 (no attacks reported): Bazarr before 1.5.7-beta.14 CVE-2026-61826 (10.0, missing auth on /api/plex/*), Thales Sentinel Keys Server before 1.3.8.0 CVE-2026-78403 (9.8, unauthenticated stack overflow), pgAdmin 4 CVE-2026-116241 (9.9, psql \copy wrapper escape), SOCFortress CoPilot CVE-2026-61728 (9.9) and JetBrains Toolbox jetbrainsd CVE-2026-118697 (9.0); update when fixes are listed. Kubeflow Pipelines also fixed a decompression bomb and unauthorized pod-log access (CVE-2026-118761, CVE-2026-118759).

Flap (crypto project) says its official website was hit by DNS hijacking on Oct 31 and sent visitors to a fake site with malicious wallet-connect prompts; don't connect wallets to it until it confirms the fix (X report).

New Oct 30 evening: fctr-id okta-ai-agent (an AI agent app for Okta admins) CVE-2026-63377 lets an unauthenticated attacker create the first admin account during setup and take over the app; update to 3.0.1-beta and don't leave a fresh install reachable before setup is finished (X report of the CVE record). A second flaw in the same app, CVE-2026-63378 (8.8, lets an attacker get at session cookies), is fixed in the same 3.0.1-beta release (X report of the NVD record).

AWS Kinesis Producer Library for Java before 1.0.8 (CVE-2026-119117): DEBUG logs and native process arguments can expose AWS credentials to local users; upgrade to 1.0.8 and rotate keys if DEBUG logging was on (X report of AWS's disclosure).

AI agents' bundled browsers: an X post warns that agent tools shipping their own cached Chromium may still be open to CVE-2026-85046, an exploited V8 type-confusion bug fixed in Chrome 152.0.7977.82; check the Chromium version your browser-use agents actually run (unverified).

AI code-scanner evasion (X post, unverified): malware authors reportedly stuff JavaScript comments with weapons terminology so AI code scanners refuse to analyze the file; don't treat an AI scanner's refusal as a clean result.

Accenture / Pentagon (WIRED, Oct 29; disputed): sources say a contractor connected a NIPRNet system holding controlled unclassified information to a personal Claude Code account, giving the agent admin access for about two months, and it appears to have sent login credentials, passwords and a network map to a third-party site NIST had flagged as high risk. Accenture says an independent investigation found the allegations without merit; the Pentagon declined to comment. Don't give AI agents your own login or admin credentials, and block unapproved agent accounts on sensitive networks.

Flowise CVE-2026-119978 (9.0, published Oct 30): with ALLOW_BUILTIN_DEP=true, any logged-in user can escape the vm2 sandbox through /api/v1/node-custom-function and run OS commands; affects Flowise through 3.1.4. Turn ALLOW_BUILTIN_DEP off and update once a fixed release is listed. No attacks reported. Also new: pybars3 through 0.9.7 CVE-2026-119716 (9.2) lets Handlebars template authors run Python code.

Linux kernel CVE-2026-98432 (moved off the focus list; lab-only AI-built zero-click remote root exploit, no attacks reported): move internet-facing servers to a fixed kernel (5.10.272, 5.15.223, 6.1.190, 6.6.159, 6.12.113, 6.18.56, 7.2.10 or 7.3+) or your distro's patched build and reboot, multipath TCP listeners first. As of Nov 1 Ubuntu (all releases 'work in progress' or vulnerable) and RHEL 8, 9 and 10 still have no fixed kernel; Debian, Oracle Linux UEK, some SUSE and some Amazon Linux builds are fixed. Until then, disable or firewall MPTCP if you don't use it; an X post also suggests dropping IPv4 TCP packets that carry IP options (unverified as a complete mitigation). Update (madrobot.blog, Nov 1 evening, citing an advisory from Atlas): Ubuntu's tracker still listed all its kernels as vulnerable and Red Hat was still 'expediting' fixes; Atlas counted 36 GitHub repositories referencing the CVE, at least six claiming a race trigger or proof of concept (not verified). Find MPTCP listeners with ss -Mlnp and patch those hosts first.

OpenCode and MCP Inspector (CVE-2026-119025, root cause in the 'open' npm package 7.2.0 before 11.0.0): on Windows and WSL, a malicious MCP server's OAuth sign-in URL with $(...) runs PowerShell on your machine before any tool is listed (OpenCode 1.0.137-1.18.32, MCP Inspector 2.0-2.11). Update both and only connect to MCP servers you trust.

InternLM LMDeploy CVE-2026-119706 (9.8, published Oct 30): versions 0.9.0 through 0.18.0 run attacker commands from a pickle sent to the unauthenticated /update_weights endpoint; keep LMDeploy API servers off the internet and update once a fix is listed. No attacks reported.
n8n CVE-2026-119408 (8.8): users who can create or import workflows can run JavaScript in the main process through hidden Function and LangChain Code nodes; update to 2.42.6, 2.43.3 or 3.0.1.

TianoCore EDK II CVE-2026-97631 (critical, found by Anthropic and Google researchers per SecurityWeek/Ars Technica): an oversized ICMP error during PXE network boot can hang or run code in UEFI firmware on most servers; it went public early after AMI shipped a fix. Ask your server vendor for firmware updates and turn off PXE boot where unused.

Trezor (BleepingComputer, Oct 30): credible reports of a suspected crypto-theft hardware implant in a Trezor Safe 5 sold by reseller CryptoBilis in Southeast Asia; buy hardware wallets only from the maker or authorized sellers and check tamper seals.

New breaches Oct 30: Hyundai Easywell (abnormal API access leaked client-company members' names, birth dates, phones and emails), GS E&C (apartment amenity booking system, residents' details and passwords), University of Copenhagen (about 525,000 people incl. CPR numbers; ~20,000 ID-card PINs reissued), ENGIE France (customer data via a sales-partner tool), and AU Small Finance Bank investigating a claimed Salesforce-hosted vehicle-loan data leak (claim by 'Scarlett Group' unverified).

AI-run attacks in this week's SecurityWeek roundup: Cisco Talos describes NIK C2, a new AI-integrated command-and-control framework with a credential-stealing, keylogging and screen-locking Windows implant; Sophos' earlier Aur0ra ransomware report (GOLD OGRE using Cursor-orchestrated agents for discovery and lateral movement) was also re-highlighted. Help Net Security (Nov 2) adds that GOLD OGRE got past AI guardrails by calling intrusions authorized red teaming or diagnostics, used Cursor's Composer plus Anthropic, xAI and Moonshot models, and that three victims where agents reached domain admin were later named on Aur0ra's leak site.
SGLang (AI inference engine): Cloudflare's GLM 5.3 cross-tenant leak came partly from an SGLang bug with over-length requests; if you serve models with SGLang, update to 0.5.22 or later.
n0n extortion group (SOCRadar, Oct 28; moved off the focus list): built its attack toolkit with the opencode AI coding agent; 93 victims listed. See the AI activity roll-up.

Pentagon freezer probe: officials now suspect Iran-linked hackers caused freezer failures at about six US military commissaries starting in late August (Nextgov via SecurityWeek); French investigators are involved after similar refrigeration-control hacks at about 350 French sites.

Unauthorized Codex / Claude Code relay (Symantec, Oct 29): a service seen at about a dozen organizations, mostly in mainland China, installs the genuine tools from scripts on lookalike domains such as vibe.aiok[.]me, then points ~/.codex/config.toml or ~/.claude/settings.json at its own servers, sets Codex sandbox_mode to danger-full-access and turns off telemetry. It can see prompts, files and secrets; no data theft confirmed. Check those config files for unknown base_url / ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL values.

TeamViewer CVE-2026-111585 (8.8, Remedio): a malicious or compromised host can crash or run code on the technician's viewer through an oversized screen surface; fixed in TeamViewer 15.83 (plus legacy builds and fixes for CVE-2026-92372 and macOS CVE-2026-92374). No attacks reported; update clients and Remote Management add-ons.

Rank Math PRO 3.0.123 (WordPress SEO plugin): an X post says this release shipped compromised (single source, unverified); if you run it, check for an official notice before updating and look for unexpected admin users or files.

New critical CVEs (Oct 30, no attacks reported): vsftpd through 3.0.5 CVE-2026-119568 (9.1, FTPS data-connection hijack via TLS session-ticket resumption) and CakePHP through 5.4.3 CVE-2026-119418/119419 (9.2, SQL injection in window-function and collation values); update when fixes ship.

testmetest npm worm (moved off the focus list): 42 hijacked GitHub repos carry .claude, .gemini, .cursor and .vscode start-up hooks that run a disguised .github/init.js; a watchdog wipes the home folder if the stolen GitHub token is revoked, so stop the net-health-checker service before revoking tokens from a clean machine.

Gravity Forms CVE-2026-103039 (CVSS 9.8, published Oct 30): PHP object injection through a List-type Post Custom Field in all versions through 3.1.2; update Gravity Forms past 3.1.2 as soon as a fixed release is available. No attacks reported.

AI Engine WordPress plugin CVE-2026-110732 (through 3.8.6): its MCP module's OAuth client-registration endpoint is open to anyone, so an unauthenticated attacker can register an active OAuth client; update the plugin or turn off its MCP module.

AWS DynamoDB MCP server (awslabs.dynamodb-mcp-server, AWS bulletin 2026-097, CVE-2026-85654): MCP schema names were pasted into generated CDK code, allowing code injection; update the package per AWS's bulletin (X report).

So-net / Plala (Sony's Japanese ISPs): about 2.6 million subscriber records taken Oct 19, plus about 54,000 email-service passwords, which were reset Oct 27 (SecurityWeek). Expect phishing aimed at these customers.
Bithumb finalized its Oct 27 groupware breach: 6,444 customers (844 with ID numbers and ID copies directly exposed) and 715 employees; exchange accounts and assets were not touched, per the company.
Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN CVE-2026-20127: an X post ties the exploitation to Volt Typhoon's 'Silent Train' network (unverified; earlier reporting named UAT-11473).

GoDaddy / 123 Reg (UK registrar): customers are being told a Sep 18 intrusion read names, phone numbers, VAT numbers, account and product details through an API; the company calls it its first AI-driven attack, says the attackers' servers in China and Singapore held copied Anthropic attack skills and ties it to the ARTEX agent (the company's own attribution). Expect targeted phishing; turn on two-step verification.

Shadow AI leaks: Johns Hopkins Bayview is notifying 3,182 patients after a staffer uploaded a patient spreadsheet to an unapproved public AI tool (found Sep 21), and RIZAP put 726 insurance members' health records into a personal AI chat account in August. Block unapproved AI uploads of regulated data.

Fake Solana starter kit (Air Security via BleepingComputer, Oct 29): GitHub repo SolanaUpdateTools/solana-starter-kit ranks top when AI coding agents search for a Solana template; its README's only step is a PowerShell one-liner that installs NetSupport RAT. Don't let agents run install commands from READMEs without review.

Drupal Commerce Core CVE-2026-118539 (highly critical access bypass, exploited per Drupal's SA-CONTRIB-2026-254; moved off the focus list): upgrade to Commerce Core 3.3.13 or 8.x-2.41 and audit recent orders for altered prices or totals.

Sophos UTM CVE-2026-118633 (critical, disclosed Oct 28): with email-proxy scanning on, an unauthenticated attacker can win a race condition by repeating requests and run code as root; UTM is end-of-life, so update to 9.724 and install Sophos's manual cssd patch per its advisory (no attacks reported).

Progress WS_FTP Server: an X post flags a CVSS 10 unauthenticated admin-credential exposure (CVE-2026-84295) plus OS command injection (CVE-2026-90868, CVE-2026-90865), patched; check Progress's advisory and update (details unverified here).

Padre Terminal: a fake crypto trading app that was on Apple's App Store is linked to about $23,000 stolen from 27 Solana wallets (BleepingComputer, Oct 29); delete it and move funds from any wallet you connected.

atlisp/mcp 1.12.14 on npm (GHSA-65cr-mcfq-59hh): an X post says this MCP server release shipped malware; if an AI agent launched it, treat the machine as compromised and rotate its credentials (single source).

FreeSWITCH CVE-2026-116779 (exploited; a single SIP MESSAGE runs server commands): upgrade to 1.11.3 and turn on ice_verify_message_integrity, or set enable-chat=false, remove passwordless directory users and set disable_system_api_commands=true (moved off the focus list).

Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN CVE-2026-20127 (exploited by UAT-11473 to plant KeyDrift, BleepingComputer Oct 29): upgrade Controller/Manager/Validator to 20.18.2.1, 20.15.4.2, 20.12.5.3/20.12.6.1 or 20.9.8.2 and review peering logs for unknown peers (moved off the focus list).

GitHub issue-injection campaign (Radware via The Register, Oct 29): on Sep 1, 74 likely hijacked accounts posted 83 issues, PRs and comments with commands hidden in HTML comments to 61 public repos (including Trivy, MLflow, agno, CopilotKit, qwen-code, Brave and Homebrew cask), aiming at GitHub Actions workflows that paste issue or PR text into shell steps to steal CI secrets; two runs executed. Check your workflows for ${{ github.event.* }} values used directly in run: steps and rotate CI secrets if any ran.

Oracle PeopleSoft: the zero-day ShinyHunters exploited since about May turns out to be three chained flaws (PSIGW SSRF, PSEMHUB file write, XML deserialization; CVE-2026-35273 patched in June), and attackers bypassed WAF rules with /%50SEMHUB/. Apply Oracle's fixes and block PSIGW/PSEMHUB from the internet (The Hacker News, Google Cloud).

Crypto platforms (Oct 29): Indodax paused all deposits and withdrawals after a jump in attack attempts and says no funds or data were taken; South Korea's Prabang lost about KRW 100 million (about $70,000) from its hot wallet and suspended service; Initia reportedly lost $2.7 million to a MoveVM token-minting exploit (X report, unverified).

Coinbase says analytics vendor Amplitude exposed contact details of a small subset of customers (its own systems weren't breached), so expect convincing fake support calls; blockchain-data provider Allium revoked all API keys after unauthorized access on Oct 25: create new keys, reset passwords and turn on MFA.
Telegram for Android: NebuSec says an attacker could run code on a phone when the victim answered an ordinary voice call (The Hacker News, Oct 29); keep Telegram updated.

Yoba campaign (The Hacker News, Oct 29, confirming Check Point's earlier X post): fake ChatGPT and Claude desktop apps on GitHub bundle the real signed OpenAI or Anthropic installer with loaders and an XMRig miner; download AI apps only from the vendor's own site.

AI agent frameworks published Oct 28-29: a batch of IBM Langflow OSS CVEs up to 9.9 (code execution and auth bypass through 1.12.8; an X post says they are fixed in Langflow 1.13.0), agno CVE-2026-119050 (prompt injection to code execution via PandasTools, through 3.1.11, no patch listed), llama.cpp ggml-rpc crash CVE-2026-119052 and Crawl4AI CVE-2026-119120; X posts also flag Claude Agent SDK CVE-2026-96620 (9.2, untrusted session IDs passed to resume can load an attacker MCP config) and vLLM 0.32.0 fixing 8 CVEs (details unverified here). An X post (Oct 29) says a proof-of-concept for Langflow auth bypass CVE-2026-93680 is on GitHub (unverified). Also: Strands Agents Tools CVE-2026-115415 lets an LLM turn off secret masking through a tool parameter, so prompt injection could expose host credentials; upgrade (X post, Oct 30).

Rocket.new (AI app builder) breach: an attacker took encrypted third-party API keys, including AI provider keys, for about 0.2% of users on Oct 27; revoke and replace any keys you connected (moved off the focus list).
Citysourced (civic issue-reporting platform used by local governments): an X report claims a 42 million-record exposure including personal data (unverified).

Command Code (AI coding agent built for open models): says it detected and stopped a security incident tied to a large-scale distillation attack on Anthropic and OpenAI models and revoked all customer API keys as a precaution; it says no users are known to be affected and it is investigating with Cloudflare, Anthropic and OpenAI (company post on X, Oct 28-29). Log in to Command Code Studio for a new key, run `cmd login`, and replace COMMAND_CODE_API_KEY in shells and CI.
Adobe Commerce / Magento PolyShell CVE-2026-48356 (CISA KEV, hundreds of stores breached with a hidden loader): apply Adobe's APSB26-73 fix and check for planted files (moved off the focus list).

iRhythm (heart-monitoring devices): an HHS filing puts its breach at 8.2 million people; hackers took personal information and account and device data from third-party-hosted business applications (SecurityWeek, Oct 29).
Arara Message (Japanese bulk email service, Paycloud Holdings): about 3.01 million email addresses taken through a web-server vulnerability on Oct 28; the service is suspended with no restart date.

Other confirmed breaches (Oct 29): Jin Air (1,454 members' data), TFG London, owner of Hobbs and Whistles (customer and employee data may have been accessed), and Eurofiber France (breach via its ticketing system; ByteToBreach's claim of data on about 10,000 business clients is unverified).
Wagyu (crypto exchange): confirmed a three-month data leak that could weaken Monero (XMR) users' privacy (single X/ForkLog report, details unverified).

Broadcom VMware ESXi CVE-2026-41709 (CISA KEV, added Oct 28): a low-scored (2.7) flaw that lets someone with ESXi admin access run certain commands without them being logged; CrowdStrike says China-nexus WARP PANDA used it as a zero-day as late as early 2026 against US organizations including law firms. Patch to ESXi 9.1.0.0 build 25370933, 9.0.2.0100 build 25595025 or 8.0 U3j build 25429389 (VMSA-2026-0006), and treat ESXi admin credentials as high-value.

Myrealtrip (South Korean travel platform, Oct 29): reports unauthorized access exposing names, phone numbers, encrypted passwords and some passport numbers; it blocked the access and notified authorities. Bithumb now says 6,444 customers were affected by the hack of an internal employee system, 844 with personal data directly exposed (X reports, Oct 29).

RMS Cloud (hotel and holiday-park booking software) breach is now confirmed: guests of Australian hotels, including Federal Group properties in Tasmania, are getting convincing phishing that quotes real booking numbers; RMS says payment details were not accessed (ABC News, Oct 29). Don't pay or click links in booking messages; contact the hotel directly.

ConnectWise Cloud Backup / Storm-0940 (ARTEX AI agents): if you use ConnectWise Cloud Backup or an MSP with app access to your Microsoft 365 tenant, review Entra enterprise apps and service principals for credentials, owners or roles added since Oct 15, and sign-ins from 144.172.64[.]99 (moved off the focus list; no new details).

Cathedral's AI agents reached Anthropic's sales, HR and IT systems through unnamed third-party business software in under 12 hours; Anthropic says no conversations, code or model weights were touched. Review scopes and admin accounts of sales, HR and IT SaaS An X post (Oct 29) claims Cathedral got full admin access to Anthropic's Slack workspace; Anthropic's Logan Graham has called claims of reading every message and logging in as any user wrong, so treat it as disputed (moved off the focus list; vendors still unnamed).

DHS employee data leak (Oct 28): a hacker calling itself 'Department of Peace' published names, job titles and work contacts of 40,000+ DHS staff (about 21,000 CBP, 10,000 ICE/HSI, ~1,000 CISA), saying it came from DHS's Okta single sign-on system; TechCrunch and Reuters matched part of it to real records. DHS has not confirmed how it was taken. Expect targeted phishing of federal staff. An X post (Oct 30) says Okta reports seeing no compromise of its own systems (unverified).

Amadeus airline reservation breach (Malaysia Airlines joined on Nov 1; Edaily tallies at least 184,000 affected records across airlines): attackers using credentials for an account in Amadeus's passenger service system accessed reservation data from Aug 2023 to Sep 2026. Japan Airlines about 92,000 customers (about 2,000 with passport numbers), ANA about 37,800, Cathay Pacific about 53,000 bookings, Jin Air 1,454; Korean Air, Asiana and Condor also affected. No card data. Travellers should watch for airline-themed phishing.
South Korea (Yonhap, Oct 28): Daishin Securities (38,490 customers' names, emails and phone numbers), Mirae Asset Global Investments and crypto exchange Bithumb reported customer data breaches.

Fake AI crawler scanner (Cequence CQ Prime, Oct 28): since late September a scanner rotating through 32 fake AI bot identities (OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Perplexity and others) has requested about 90 paths holding config files, cloud credentials and SSH keys; it reached 48% of Cequence-protected organizations on one day, mostly blocked. Don't allowlist traffic by AI user-agent alone and make sure .env, cloud credential and key files are never web-served.
Gitee (China's largest Git host): an X post claims 26,400 live credentials (database strings, API keys, cloud tokens) are exposed in public repos (single X post, unverified).

Warp says an AI 'agent swarm' broke in through a vendor and read agent trace and telemetry data of up to ~1% of users: If you use Warp, watch for a notice from Warp and follow its instructions. If your Warp agent sessions ever printed or handled secrets (API keys, tokens, .env values, cloud credentials), rotate them, since agent traces can contain command output. Nothing to update on your side yet.

Railway platform breach: ~100,000 workspaces' secrets possibly decrypted, attacker hunting AI keys: Anyone who stored secrets on Railway before Oct 21: rotate every env var and revoke old keys at the issuing provider (AI keys first, then database, registry, cloud, Stripe and GitHub tokens), create new Railway API/project tokens, reconnect GitHub and redeploy bucket services, remove public network access to databases, and check provider usage, GitHub and registry audit logs back to Oct 20. If a provider revoked a replacement key, create a new one, update the Railway variable and redeploy; this does not mean the replacement was compromised.

Comet Opik (AI evaluation platform, Oct 24-26): an attacker used an inactive account's API key and a flaw in Opik's AI provider settings to obtain 29 of Comet's internal OpenAI and Anthropic keys; Comet says no customer data, accounts or keys were accessed, revoked the keys and now requires the key to be re-entered when a provider address changes. If you self-host Opik or store provider keys in similar tools, update, restrict provider endpoints and watch provider usage.

Sony Network Communications (So-net, Japan): attackers took 2,585,481 customer records on Oct 19 (names, phone numbers, emails, user IDs, birth dates, gender, connection IDs) and the passwords of 54,401 email accounts, which Sony reset on Oct 27; 443,495 of the records are NTT Docomo plala (S Course) customers. Expect phishing; affected users should set new passwords via So-net My Page.

MLflow CVE-2026-116692 (CVSS 9.8, RCE) and CVE-2026-116690 (7.5, arbitrary file read): both work against default no-auth MLflow tracking servers; upgrade to MLflow 3.17.0 and put authentication in front of the server. A single X post claims CVE-2026-116690 is exploited, but GitHub's advisory, Feedly and TheHackerWire show no confirmed exploitation or KEV listing (unverified).

Langflow CVE-2026-105740: MCP stdio command injection lets any authenticated user run shell commands; ZoomEye counts about 19,200 exposed instances. Update Langflow and don't expose it to the internet (no attacks reported).
US Federal Election Commission took its electronic filing system offline on Oct 26 after an attempted breach (X report; details unconfirmed).

Oracle E-Business Suite CVE-2026-101767 (CVSS 9.8, unauthenticated SQL injection leading to RCE in the TCF servlet /OA_HTML/AppsTCFServer, EBS 12.2.3-12.2.15, found by Horizon3.ai): Defused's decoys logged the first exploratory attempts on Oct 27, about a week after Oracle's Oct 20 Critical Patch Update fixed it; an X post on Oct 29 repeats Defused's report of exploratory exploit traffic; no confirmed intrusions yet. Apply the October CPU (MOS Note KA923); until then remove /OA_HTML/AppsTCFServer from the EBS URL firewall allowlist, restrict the web tier to trusted networks, and look for unauthenticated POSTs to that path invoking GanttDataServer and oracle-account shells from the Concurrent Manager.
Gotenberg CVE-2026-40281 (exploited ExifTool argument injection dropping a Go reverse shell): upgrade to 8.31.0+, keep it off the internet and check hosts running it (moved off the focus list).

Skyw4lker device-code phishing (ANY.RUN via The Hacker News, Oct 28): a campaign mostly against US organizations abuses Microsoft's device-code sign-in flow to take over corporate accounts without stealing passwords; block device-code flow with Conditional Access where it isn't needed.

Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 (9.8, in CISA KEV): ZDI says the zero-day ShinyHunters has exploited since May (mostly universities, then a wider September wave across tech, healthcare, government and more) is three chained flaws: an SSRF in the Integration Gateway reaches the Environment Management Hub because 127.0.0.1 is trusted by default, then a log-write command plants a web shell or an XMLDecoder file runs code on restart. Attackers bypassed WAF rules by requesting /%50SEMHUB/. Apply Oracle's June 10 security alert fix for PeopleTools 8.61/8.62, or disable/remove PSEMHUB; if exposed, hunt for web shells and rotate credentials reachable from the PeopleSoft tier, since patching doesn't evict an intruder.

Fortinet FortiSIEM CVE-2026-106173 (9.4, unauthenticated RCE via gRPC on TCP 27918, public PoC, exploitation reported by Canada's Cyber Centre, not yet in CISA KEV): upgrade 7.5.0 to 7.5.1+ or 7.6, block TCP 27918 from untrusted hosts and check cron-run scripts such as /opt/charting/redishb.sh (moved off the focus list).

llama.cpp CVE-2026-118375 (CVSS 9.2, published Oct 28): out-of-bounds stack write in the ggml-rpc RDMA transport lets an unauthenticated peer crash a llama.cpp rpc-server or possibly run code; builds b8841 up to b11865 are affected. Update to b11865 or later and never expose rpc-server to untrusted networks. No attacks reported.

Veeam Backup & Replication CVE-2026-108142 (CVSS 9.1, published Oct 27): unauthenticated authorization bypass in the CDP Coordinator Service on v13.0 and 13.1 (12.x not affected). No attacks reported, but Veeam servers are a favorite ransomware target; upgrade to 13.1.2.57 or 13.0.3.63 and restrict network access to the CDP Coordinator (Veeam KB4948).

NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit CVE-2026-65145 (CVSS 10.0, missing authentication, may allow code execution) affects 1.0 to 1.8.0; fixed in 1.9.0 (PyPI package nvidia-nat, released Sep 10). Also CVE-2026-65151 SQL injection fixed in 1.7.0. No attacks reported (NVIDIA bulletin 5912, Oct 27).

Aokigahara infostealer (Check Point, Oct 27): steals session and config files for Claude Code/Desktop, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, ChatGPT Desktop, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot and Gemini CLI, plus Git, SSH and cloud credentials. If a developer machine was infected, sign out of and revoke those AI tool sessions and rotate keys from a clean device.

EPICS Base (control software for particle accelerators and fusion experiments): Causal Security's autonomous agent Cipher found four flaws in under four hours, including critical CVE-2026-114595 (9.8, heap write, possible RCE); CISA advisory Oct 27; update to EPICS 7.0.11. No attacks reported.

Convertr: a card-skimming group reportedly compromised a shared analytics script used by the e-commerce platform to steal shoppers' card data at checkout (BleepingComputer, Oct 27). If your store loads Convertr scripts, check what they serve and watch for card fraud reports.

Cairn AI agents broke into websites of 100+ companies (Deere, SharkNinja, Cummins vendor), Reuters reports, using a mix of DeepSeek and Claude Code at about $50 per successful hack; patch e-commerce sites and admin panels and watch for web shells (moved off the focus list; no new details).

Fortinet patched critical flaws found by frontier AI testing in FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator, with details withheld until Nov 10; apply the October updates now (moved off the focus list; no new details).

Tailscale: v1.104.4 was published on GitHub at 01:05 UTC Oct 28 (9:05 PM EDT Oct 27), and Tailscale's security bulletins list fixes in 1.104.4 or newer, including Tailscale SSH memory exhaustion (TS-2026-015), Serve Unix backends reaching privileged sockets such as the tailscaled local API (TS-2026-016) and HTTP/2 capability mix-ups in Serve (TS-2026-017). The bulletins do not name 'Tailworm' or Cyberdione Labs, so whether all 11 Tailworm findings are covered is not confirmed. Update clients to 1.104.4 now; keep TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING=1 and tight SSH rules until Tailscale confirms full coverage; headscale up to 0.29.6 was also listed as affected. No exploitation reported.

AI/MCP tool command-injection batch (published Oct 27, CVSS up to 8.5, no attacks reported): ai-sdlc plugin MCP server through 0.31.2 (CVE-2026-117558), DroidMind through 0.4.0 (CVE-2026-117559), ATXP Gemini CLI extension through 1.0.0 (CVE-2026-117560), sf-mcp through 1.3.2 (CVE-2026-117561), esp-mcp (CVE-2026-117567), mcp-ffmpeg through 1.0.5 (CVE-2026-117568), Kali-GPT (CVE-2026-117569) and hagent (CVE-2026-117573); also an unbounded request-size flaw in the official MCP TypeScript SDK HTTP transports (GHSA-f897-62hf-6gxq) and LiteLLM file read and XSS advisories (GHSA-g5ff-637f-6q2m, GHSA-hhww-mrg2-969h). Update or remove these tools.

Adobe Campaign Classic: several critical flaws published Oct 27, including SQL injection CVE-2026-105781 (CVSS 10.0) and code-execution bugs CVE-2026-105489, -105780, -104351 and -104353 (9.9); Adobe Connect CVE-2026-48360 (9.6) code injection. No attacks reported; apply Adobe's updates.

LiteLLM 1.107.0 backdoored on PyPI and Docker after a leaked AI-agent platform key (AI supply chain): If 1.107.0 (or the latest, main-latest or main-stable images on Oct 21) was installed, pulled or mirrored: don't run python or pip in that environment; investigate from a clean machine, delete cook.pth, cook.py and sitecustomize.py or better rebuild images and venvs, pin 1.106.2 by digest, and rotate every reachable credential from a clean machine (provider keys in the proxy DB, master and virtual keys, DATABASE_URL, cloud roles, CI, registry and Git tokens). Block litellm[.]dev. No CVE has been assigned. (moved off the focus list; no new details).

Bubble no-code platform breach: attacker took some users' API Connector and plugin credentials: If you build on Bubble: rotate every third-party API key or token stored in API Connector calls and plugins (payment, email, CRM, AI provider keys), check those services' usage logs since Oct 26, and set your app editor to 'Private app' unless it must be public. Plugin developers should rotate private keys stored in their plugins. Trust only messages from bubble.io and status.bubble.io. (moved off the focus list; no new details).

Treg (AI agent tools platform): an attacker ran commands on its production web service on Oct 23 via a server-side feature, apparently to steal AI inference provider keys, which treg ties to a series of attacks on platform companies. If you added your own keys (e.g. OpenRouter or other AI providers) to treg, rotate them at the provider and review October usage; all treg tokens were reset.

ENGIE (BleepingComputer, Oct 27): attackers took French customers' names, postal and email addresses, phone numbers, customer IDs, contract numbers and electricity PDL / gas PCE meter IDs from a tool partners use to sell energy offers; ENGIE says its internal systems and banking data were not affected and has not said how many customers. Expect phishing and fake 'ENGIE' calls that quote real contract details.

AfD (German party) hosting provider breach: Have I Been Pwned confirmed 345,000+ unique email addresses plus large volumes of emails and attachments taken from AfD-owned host Alternita in September (The Register, Oct 27). The attackers' claim that entry was via a poorly protected WordPress site is unverified.

DreamHost forced password resets for all email and FTP/SFTP users in a still-unexplained incident; if you host there, set new unique passwords, check mail forwarding rules and review site files changed since Oct 23 (moved off the focus list; no new details).

Gheist: stolen GitHub tokens used to plant secret-dumping 'ci-sync-*' workflow branches in 850+ accounts' repos; search for branches matching ci-sync-[0-9a-z]{6} and the 'gheist' user agent, and rotate secrets if found (moved off the focus list; no new details).

Denver Health Medical Plan: AI/ML analytics vendor SquareML left a live read-only database access key on a public website from Jun 27, 2025 to Aug 2026, exposing health data of 238,083 members to possible access; no evidence it was used (SecurityWeek, Oct 27).
Flowise CVE-2026-73487: its CSV and Airtable agents ran model-written Python after only a regex blocklist check, so a prompt could run code; fixed in Flowise 3.1.3. No attacks reported.

FortiBleed 2.0 (Infostealers.com, Oct 27): a newly obtained set of FortiGate configuration reports from around February 2026 holds 40,573 records with cleartext secrets, including 37,076 local-user and 1,576 Active Directory LDAP bind records, covering 975 domains not in the first leak. If you run FortiGate, rotate local VPN and LDAP bind passwords and check whether your domain is listed (single source).

SiteGuard Server Edition (Japanese web application firewall) CVE-2026-106931: OS command injection in the default-on statistics feature runs commands as root/SYSTEM; exploited and in CISA KEV (added Oct 20). Upgrade Apache/Nginx/IIS editions to Ver8.00 Update5 (FreeBSD to Ver7.00 Update6) per JPCERT, and preserve logs before patching.
